item.title: CV Notes
item.description: There is a lot of maths behind CV which we take for granted, this post aims to explore it. Increasing image size Deconvolution Inverse of Convolution, if we know the final image and the convolution matrix we can get the original image back using Inverse Fourier Transformation. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f-IINpceX6k UpSampling2D It is simple interpolation with no learnable parameters. It can either be nearest, which means just repeating the values or something like bilinear interpolation, bicubic, etc.

item.title: Image generation using Deep Learning
item.description: Oh GAN, here we go again. Some math background Likelihood Function If the data samples are given, what is the “likelihood” of the parameters $\theta$ of our model. Like if n coit tosses are given what is the likelihood that the p(H) = 0.5. Likelihood(L) $ L(\theta| \boldsymbol x) = P(\boldsymbol x| \theta)$ Here $\boldsymbol x$ is the observed data In MLE we find the $\theta$ that maximizes the probabilty of our observation.

item.title: Need for Speed: Optimizing Deep Learning Models
item.description: Huang et al. showed that mixed precision training is 1.5x to 5.5x faster over float32 on V100 GPUs, and an additional 1.3x to 2.5x faster on A100 GPUs on a variety of networks. On very large networks the need for mixed precision is even more evident. Narayanan et al. reports that it would take 34 days to train GPT-3 175B on 1024 A100 GPUs (with a batch size of 1536), but it’s estimated it would take over a year using float32!

item.title: Neural Architecture Search
item.description: NAS One of the key challenges in designing deep learning models is finding the task specific architecture. This involves choosing the number of layers, the number of neurons per layer, and the connections between different layers. Typically, this is done through a process of trial and error, where the researcher trains multiple architectures to find the best among. This can be time-consuming and may not always yield the best possible results.

item.title: NLP Notes (aimed to be math intensive)
Probability & Statistics
item.description: Recall, Precision & F1 score Recall (R) R = TP/(TP + FN) i.e. number of true values “recalled” out of total true values Precision (P) P = TP/(TP + FP) i.e. How precise you were in identifying positive cases. Covid RTPCR Test has high precision and low recall. This means if the test result is Covid positive, there is a high chance that it is correct but if it says negative, nothing can said with certainty.
